title: Minimum positive-word length in an indexed monoid alphabet
statement: Let $G$ be a monoid, meaning a set with associative multiplication and identity $1$, and let $I$ be a set with a family $t:I\to G$. For a finite word $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ in $I$, let $t_A=t_{a_1}\cdots t_{a_k}$, with empty product $1$. Define $\ell_t(g)=\min\{|A|:t_A=g\}$ when this set is nonempty, and define $\ell_t(g)=0$ otherwise. The same definition for the restricted family $J\to G$ gives the length in a subset $J\subseteq I$. No finiteness, injectivity, involution or presentation assumption is imposed by this definition.

source.place: Cashen, Notes on Coxeter groups, version 31 October 2023, Chapter 4, Lemma 4.0.5, printed p.118, minimal tuples in an alphabet. General positive-word minimum used in its deletion argument; value zero outside the represented submonoid is the total-function convention, never used in the consumer.
